boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named, public-facing University of Michigan destinations with documented free admission or free public access.

cards.entity_name: University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.title: Wander the UMMA galleries
cards.subtitle: 525 S. State St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Meet at the museum entrance, choose one floor to explore together, and use the gallery map to compare a few works before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A ticket-free art outing with rotating exhibitions and galleries to explore at your own pace.
cards.evidence_claim: UMMA states that tickets are not required and admission is always free for everyone.
cards.source_title: Visit – University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Public museum; check the visit page for current gallery hours. Photography is allowed without flash or tripods.

cards.title: Browse the Kelsey’s ancient-world galleries
cards.subtitle: 434 S. State St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Enter through the public Maynard Street entrance, pick a gallery theme, and use the available guide to trade observations as you move through it.
cards.short_summary: A compact archaeology museum where the permanent galleries support an unhurried, no-ticket visit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kelsey Museum says it is free and open to all, with no tickets or admission fee required.
cards.source_title: Visit – U-M LSA Kelsey Museum of Archaeology
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday and weekends; closed Mondays and university holidays. Use the public Maynard Street entrance.

cards.entity_name: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History
cards.title: See the natural-history exhibits
cards.subtitle: Biological Sciences Building · 1105 N. University Ave.
cards.notes: Start with a single exhibit hall, set a casual observation challenge, and leave time to look closely at the specimens that catch your group’s eye.
cards.short_summary: Free general museum admission makes this an easy daytime stop for science displays and collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that general admission is always free for individuals and families.
cards.source_title: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: General admission is free; separately ticketed planetarium or dome programs may have different terms. Check current seasonal hours.

cards.entity_name: Judy and Stanley Frankel Detroit Observatory
cards.title: Visit the Detroit Observatory
cards.subtitle: 1398 E. Ann St. · Hill Area
cards.notes: Check the observatory calendar, arrive through the Observatory Street entrance, and pair a visit with its history-of-astronomy programs or exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus observatory with free admission and scheduled public programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Observatory states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Open Thursdays, Fridays, and selected Saturdays; consult the calendar and listed closure dates before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Matthaei gardens
cards.subtitle: 1800 N. Dixboro Rd. · Northeast Ann Arbor
cards.notes: Choose an outdoor garden or trail loop, slow down at the seasonal plantings, and use the conservatory only when it is open that day.
cards.short_summary: A university botanical garden with outdoor gardens, trails, and a conservatory under free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Matthaei Botanical Gardens lists free admission.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free. Parking is metered, so arrive by bus, bike, or on foot to keep the outing at zero dollars; conservatory closes Mondays.

cards.title: Take a daylight walk in the Arb
cards.subtitle: 1610 Washington Hts. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Use a marked entrance and trail map, pick a short loop or riverside route, and plan to finish before sunset with a friend or group.
cards.short_summary: A 123-acre campus landscape for trails, gardens, river views, and relaxed outdoor time.
cards.evidence_claim: Nichols Arboretum says it has free admission and is free and open daily from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Free daily from sunrise to sunset. Limited parking may be metered; use a daytime visit and stay on established paths.

cards.title: Look through the Hatcher Gallery
cards.subtitle: Harlan Hatcher Graduate Library · Central Campus
cards.notes: Check the library’s current building access, then take a slow pass through the exhibition and choose one detail each person wants to discuss.
cards.short_summary: A free, public art-viewing stop inside Hatcher Graduate Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Arts describes Hatcher Gallery as free and open to all, during library hours.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to all during library hours; confirm current library access and exhibition availability before going.

cards.title: Drop into the Humanities Gallery
cards.subtitle: 202 S. Thayer St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Stop by during weekday gallery hours, take in the current installation, and use the posted artist information as a conversation starter.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery focused on art engaging social justice and humanities themes.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Arts identifies the Institute for the Humanities Gallery as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Listed gallery hours are Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify current exhibitions and building access before visiting.

cards.title: See the Lane Hall exhibit
cards.subtitle: 204 S. State St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Visit during weekday hours, read the exhibit framing before you begin, and leave a few minutes to compare what each person took from the display.
cards.short_summary: A rotating exhibit space centered on gender and sexuality themes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Institute for Research on Women and Gender states that Lane Hall exhibits are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Lane Hall – Institute for Research on Women and Gender
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; check the current exhibit listing before visiting.

cards.title: Browse art and science together
cards.subtitle: Dana Building · 440 Church St. · Central Campus
cards.notes: Go during weekday building hours, spend a few minutes with the current work, and talk through the environmental question or material it raises.
cards.short_summary: A university gallery presenting work at the intersection of art and environmental science.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Arts lists the Art & Environment Gallery as free and open to the public during building hours.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public during building hours, Monday–Friday; verify current building access before visiting.
